directives.intent: Reach 10 bases by turn 50; prefer colony pods and the formers that accelerate the next pod unless an immediate threat makes expansion unsafe.
directives.rationale: The seed-1 baseline was already below the CPU expansion slope by turn 55. This first checkpoint matches the provisional gate in docs/game-knowledge.md.

directives.intent: Double to 20 bases by turn 80; reinvest new-base production into colony pods and formers so expansion creates the capacity for the next expansion wave.
directives.rationale: A second absolute checkpoint after a bounded interval measures the slope, not merely the eventual endpoint.

directives.intent: Double to 40 bases by turn 110; keep mature bases producing expansion capacity while new bases establish growth and terraforming support.
directives.rationale: Seed-1 CPU factions reached 30-39 bases by turn 91 while the brain held 10; this checkpoint demands the same compounding regime.

directives.intent: Reach 60 bases by turn 140; sustain the reinvestment loop until the faction is expanding at the CPU frontier rather than linearly.
directives.rationale: The measured frontier at turn 143 was 43-66 CPU bases versus 12 for the brain. Sixty is a slope target grounded in that census, not a universal game-law claim.

directives.intent: Keep each producing base at a positive mineral surplus by prioritizing Formers and tile improvements before another colony pod whenever support or weak tiles have stalled production.
directives.rationale: The first compound arm chose Colony Pods in 102 of 107 late base-production decisions while 36 decisions explicitly named zero mineral surplus. Expansion targets need their production enabler in force at equal priority or they suppress it.
